text: Which crew does {name} mean? The company owns both plants, but only one sits on our side of the state line.
author: Codex writer B

text: The crew on this side of the line, {presiding}. Our vote can't change the law where the other plant sits.
author: Codex writer B

text: Start with the plant where the employee works, {presiding}. An agreement covering both plants doesn't give this state authority over both crews.
author: Codex writer B

text: Only our plants, {presiding}. That's part of my objection. The same bargaining team would have to explain different terms to crews doing the same job.
author: Codex writer B

text: Look at where each crew works, {presiding}. I'd leave our crew the same opportunity to bargain over a fee that it has now.
author: Codex writer B

text: Would {name} change what the worker pays, who gets a ballot at the hall, or both?
author: Codex writer B

text: The payment, {presiding}. Once the ban applies, the worker can turn it down and keep the job. The local still sets its rules for voting.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd give that worker a choice about the money, {presiding}. If they want to vote, they'd still have to look at the local's membership rules.
author: Codex writer B

text: The worker can stay outside the local, {presiding}. My concern is who picks up the expense when that same worker needs the contract enforced.
author: Codex writer B

text: It concerns the payment, {presiding}. Whether a nonmember gets a ratification ballot is up to the union's rules.
author: Codex writer B

text: What would {name} have the store manager do about the fee notice that's still up beside the schedule?
author: Codex writer B

text: Check when the new rule covers that agreement. Once it does, {presiding}, the notice can't tell the clerk that paying is a condition of keeping the job.
author: Codex writer B

text: Find the agreement the clerk works under and the date the ban reaches it, {presiding}. Then the store can tell the clerk when paying becomes a choice.
author: Codex writer B

text: Start with the date on the agreement, {presiding}. I oppose the change, but the clerk still deserves a notice they can rely on.
author: Codex writer B

text: Have the manager and the steward read the current agreement beside the effective date, {presiding}. The notice on the wall could still be from last year.
author: Codex writer B

text: Can {name} tell the bargaining team whether it could still make paying the fee a condition of keeping a job at the plant?
author: Codex writer B

text: Once the ban covers that agreement, no, {presiding}. The local can still ask workers to support it and the workers can say no.
author: Codex writer B

text: The local could ask for voluntary support, {presiding}. A worker who declined it could keep the job. That's what I'm voting for.
author: Codex writer B

text: That's the proposal we'd be ruling out, {presiding}. I'd rather hear what the crew and the company might offer each other across the table.
author: Codex writer B

text: They could ask the membership for money, {presiding}. They'd lose the chance to bargain for a contribution from everyone they represent.
author: Codex writer B

text: Does {name} think a vote here today gives the store permission to take a fee out of tomorrow's check?
author: Codex writer B

text: No, {presiding}. Lifting the state ban doesn't put a fee in the clerk's agreement. The parties would have to bargain for one.
author: Codex writer B

text: No, {presiding}. Ask for the agreement and the clerk's deduction authorization. Letting the local bargain for a fee doesn't sign either document.
author: Codex writer B

text: There'd still have to be an applicable agreement, {presiding}. My vote to keep the ban is about what a future agreement could require.
author: Codex writer B

text: There's no deduction just from our vote, {presiding}. I'm voting against repeal because the next contract could make a fee a condition of the job.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd like {name} to take this one from the worker's end. If I pay the fee the parties negotiate, do I get a ballot on the deal?
author: Codex writer B

text: Paying and joining are different decisions, {presiding}. You'd need the local's voting rules to answer for that worker.
author: Codex writer B

text: The local decides who's entitled to vote under its rules, {presiding}. What I want the parties to be able to discuss is who pays for representation.
author: Codex writer B

text: That's my concern, {presiding}. A worker could help pay for bargaining under an agreement and still be outside the room when the members vote.
author: Codex writer B

text: Paying for bargaining wouldn't put that worker on the voting list, {presiding}. That's one reason I'd keep the ban.
author: Codex writer B

text: How would {name} read a national contract that sets our plants apart in a paragraph of their own?
author: Codex writer B

text: Read the exception first, {presiding}. If it turns on what state law allows, both sides need to see how that language works after repeal.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd open the agreement, {presiding}. Some wording depends on state law and some names a plant outright. Which did the parties sign?
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd keep the ban, {presiding}. Hand me that contract and I'll show you the words I'd want the workers to ask about.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd have the local and the company read the exception back to the crew, {presiding}. I favor keeping the ban, but the contract wording matters whichever way we vote.
author: Codex writer B

text: If management says no when the local puts a fee on the table, what would {name} tell the steward our vote has changed?
author: Codex writer B

text: It has to hear a lawful bargaining proposal where the duty to bargain applies, {presiding}. The two sides can walk out with different positions.
author: Codex writer B

text: Management can propose different terms, {presiding}. I want the local to have a hearing at the table. I wouldn't promise it a signature.
author: Codex writer B

text: They wouldn't have to accept it, {presiding}. I'm voting to keep the ban because I don't want continued employment to depend on what they eventually agree.
author: Codex writer B

text: They don't have to sign it, {presiding}. My concern is the required fee they could agree to after they sit down.
author: Codex writer B

text: Same employer, same national agreement, different state line, {presiding}. A worker taking a transfer here ought to know that refusing a union payment won't cost them the job.
author: Codex writer B

text: Think of the person transferring in from another plant, {presiding}. They shouldn't have to pay a union fee to keep working here just because the company bargains for both plants together.
author: Codex writer B

text: Some of the crew never joined the local, {presiding}. I'd let them work the shift without having to pay it.
author: Codex writer B

text: Before you tell somebody the fee is worth their money, {presiding}, let them decide. A person can value the contract and still want a choice about paying the local.
author: Codex writer B

text: A new clerk reads about the fee before they've even learned where to clock in. I'd like them to know they can say no to that payment and still report for work, {presiding}.
author: Codex writer B

text: Let the new hire ask the steward what the local does and decide whether it's worth paying for, {presiding}. They shouldn't have to decide to keep their shift.
author: Codex writer B

text: Leave pay and hours on the bargaining table, {presiding}. I draw the line at an agreement that makes somebody pay the union to stay employed.
author: Codex writer B

text: If the company and the local both sign off on a fee, who speaks for the worker who doesn't want to pay it, {presiding}? I'd give that worker a choice.
author: Codex writer B

text: Somebody will have to bring this vote back to crews covered by the same national agreement, {presiding}, and explain why the terms can differ from one plant to the next.
author: Codex writer B

text: Talk to the workers outside either plant, {presiding}. They know what they gave up to get the last contract. I'd leave them room to make the next bargain.
author: Codex writer B

text: A nonmember can still need help getting the contract honored. Who pays for that work, {presiding}? I'd leave room for the two sides to settle it.
author: Codex writer B

text: When a nonmember brings in a grievance, the steward still has a job to do, {presiding}. I wouldn't take payment for that work off the table.
author: Codex writer B

text: A night clerk deserves the same explanation as the people who made the meeting, {presiding}. Fix the notice. That doesn't require a ban on fees.
author: Codex writer B

text: There's a fair question about what the store tells a new employee, {presiding}. My answer would be to show them the agreement and explain the fee. I'd vote against a ban.
author: Codex writer B

text: How do we know the crew would turn the proposal down, {presiding}? I want the negotiators to be able to hear it before they give their answer.
author: Codex writer B

text: Management can already tell the union it doesn't want that term, {presiding}. I see no reason for us to cut off the discussion before they meet.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd let the parties reopen the fee question, {presiding}. Somebody still has to read the national agreement and find out exactly which words apply to our plant.
author: Codex writer B

text: Different plants can have different terms, {presiding}. I'd repeal the ban so the crews here can bargain over their own.
author: Codex writer B

text: A nonmember may need the same help as a member when management ignores the contract. I'd let the parties talk about who pays for that work, {presiding}.
author: Codex writer B

text: Who picks up the cost when a nonmember needs representation? Let the local and the employer sit down with that question, {presiding}. That's a reason to repeal.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'm for repeal, {presiding}, and I'd like the person working nights at the grocery to get a straight explanation of any fee the parties actually negotiate.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd let the two sides negotiate, {presiding}. Then a clerk who sees a notice about fees could ask both sides to show where the agreement says it.
author: Codex writer B

text: Let the local put a fee proposal in front of the plant manager, {presiding}. Management may turn it down. I want that conversation to be possible.
author: Codex writer B

text: Let the employer bring a counteroffer, {presiding}. As long as the state bars the fee, neither side has a reason to work out terms for one.
author: Codex writer B

text: Before we lift the ban, show the crew the exception in the agreement they're working under, {presiding}. That national deal may run for years yet.
author: Codex writer B

text: I don't want a transfer to another plant in this state to start a hunt through the union contract for a fee, {presiding}. I'd keep the ban.
author: Codex writer B

text: A worker can pay for bargaining and still have no vote when the result is put to the local, {presiding}. I'd keep payment a choice.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd protect the person who doesn't join, {presiding}. Access to the contract matters to that worker, and so does being able to decline the fee.
author: Codex writer B

text: A notice goes up and the clerk has to figure out whether the next paycheck will cover the groceries. I'd keep the state ban, {presiding}, so that worker has a choice about paying.
author: Codex writer B

text: A new hire should know they can turn down a union payment and come back to work the next day, {presiding}. I won't vote to take that protection away.
author: Codex writer B

text: People keep saying a fee would have to be negotiated. That's true, {presiding}. It doesn't reassure me about the worker who objects after both sides sign.
author: Codex writer B

text: The first offer won't necessarily be the one they sign, {presiding}. I'd keep the ban because the deal they finally reach could make a fee a condition of employment.
author: Codex writer B

text: Say a worker lives in {place} and crosses the state line for a shift. Which side of the line counts?
author: Codex writer B

text: Suppose payroll gets one set of instructions for every mill, including one in {place}. How would it tell which crews our vote covers?
author: Codex writer B

text: The worker transfers across the state line and the same company signs the check. Which state's fee rule would {name} apply at the new plant?
author: Codex writer B

text: When a worker in {place} pays toward the contract and gets no say on it, which part of that deal can we change here?
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd like to hear {name} explain what the worker can do about the fee and what they'd still have to do to get a ballot.
author: Codex writer B

text: What could {name} say to the worker who pays for bargaining and waits outside while the local votes?
author: Codex writer B

text: Imagine starting a shift in {place} with last year's fee notice still on the wall. How can you tell whether you owe what it says?
author: Codex writer B

text: What would {name} put beside that notice before asking the manager and the steward to sign a new one?
author: Codex writer B

text: The clerk stays on when the old agreement ends. When would {name} tell payroll the clerk can turn the fee down?
author: Codex writer B

text: Say I'm bargaining for a crew in {place}. What could I still ask the company to put in writing about the union fee?
author: Codex writer B

text: What would {name} tell a steward who still wants everybody on the crew to chip in for bargaining?
author: Codex writer B

text: A worker in {place} says they'd rather keep the money. Once the ban covers the contract, can the manager send them home for that?
author: Codex writer B

text: Friday is payday. If a clerk in {place} calls about a new deduction, could the store point to our vote as permission to take it?
author: Codex writer B

text: Would {name} take a clerk showing up for tonight's shift as consent to a deduction if the ban is gone?
author: Codex writer B

text: What would {name} say to a clerk who thinks repeal automatically puts a deduction on the next check?
author: Codex writer B

text: Picture somebody in {place} who chipped in for the bargaining. When the steward passes out ballots on the deal, does that worker get one?
author: Codex writer B

text: Who does {name} think should answer the worker who pays a fee and asks the local for a ballot on the contract?
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd like {name} to follow the worker as far as the union hall. Would a pay stub showing the fee get them into the contract vote?
author: Codex writer B

text: If a steward in {place} called about the exception in the national agreement, which paragraph would you have them read over the phone?
author: Codex writer B

text: Two crews might work under the same contract a long way apart. How could the crew in {place} tell if its exception lasts past repeal?
author: Codex writer B

text: Which words would {name} have the steward look for in the paragraph that sets our state apart?
author: Codex writer B

text: Suppose {name} were answering a letter from the local. Would management owe the local a meeting about the fee or a signature agreeing to it?
author: Codex writer B

text: Would {name} tell the local it can collect what it asked for as soon as management has heard the proposal?
author: Codex writer B

text: The negotiators come home to {place} with a fee on the agenda. Can they tell the crew the company has agreed to it?
author: Codex writer B

text: How far across the state line does {name} think our vote follows a company that runs a mill on either side?
author: Codex writer B

text: If a neighbor in {place} said they paid but had to wait outside while the local voted, what difference would our vote make to them?
author: Codex writer B

text: What would {name} want the clerk to read before trusting the notice hanging beside the schedule?
author: Codex writer B

text: Put yourself on a crew in {place} under a contract the ban covers. If you turn down the fee, can the company fire you for it?
author: Codex writer B

text: What would {name} ask payroll to show the clerk before the store takes a fee from the next check?
author: Codex writer B

text: How should a steward in {place} answer a nonmember who paid toward bargaining and now wants a vote on the contract?
author: Codex writer B

text: Before the crew in {place} hears that its exception is gone, what would you want to know about the agreement?
author: Codex writer B

text: Management says the fee costs too much. Could the negotiators go back to {place} without a deal even if we repeal the ban?
author: Codex writer B

text: Start with where the crew works, {presiding}. I want the person clocking in here covered even when the company has its headquarters across the line.
author: Codex writer B

text: The plant here would come under our rule when its agreement is covered, {presiding}. The company putting its name on both gates doesn't change where the work is done.
author: Codex writer B

text: Which plant does the worker report to? That's where I'd start, {presiding}. I oppose putting the crew here under a different rule from their bargaining partners across the line.
author: Codex writer B

text: At the plant over the line they'd need to look up the law there, {presiding}. That's the difference I'd have to explain to a worker taking a transfer.
author: Codex writer B

text: Once their agreement is covered, they could refuse the fee and stay at work, {presiding}. For a ballot they'd still have to look at the local's voting rules.
author: Codex writer B

text: Cross the required fee off the list, {presiding}. The union keeps its own rules for handing out ballots.
author: Codex writer B

text: It changes the payment, {presiding}. The local keeps its voting rules. I'm concerned that the people enforcing the contract could lose some of the money that pays for the work.
author: Codex writer B

text: No new ballot, {presiding}. The worker could decline the fee and still go to the steward for help. That's the trade I think the member should explain.
author: Codex writer B

text: Lay the notice next to the contract, {presiding}, and find out when the new rule applies. That's the point when the clerk can keep the job without paying the fee.
author: Codex writer B

text: Check when the ban applies to that agreement, {presiding}. If the notice says everybody has to pay and the payment is now voluntary, take it down.
author: Codex writer B

text: What dates does the notice actually cover, {presiding}? I'd vote against the ban, but I wouldn't tell a clerk what they owe from last year's notice.
author: Codex writer B

text: The steward and the store have the same contract to look at, {presiding}. They need its dates and the start date of the new rule before they answer that clerk.
author: Codex writer B

text: When the ban reaches the agreement, keeping the job can't depend on paying the local, {presiding}. The local could still ask the worker to contribute.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd leave the worker free to chip in, {presiding}, including the worker who thinks the steward earned every penny. The contract couldn't make that payment compulsory once the ban applies.
author: Codex writer B

text: They could ask workers for voluntary support, {presiding}. What they couldn't negotiate is a requirement that everyone represented pay as a condition of keeping the job.
author: Codex writer B

text: A request for help with costs could still go to each worker, {presiding}. The negotiators would lose the option of writing a required fee into a covered contract. I'd leave them that option.
author: Codex writer B

text: Payroll needs more than our vote, {presiding}. Who signed the deduction authorization? Reopening a subject for bargaining doesn't give the store a signature from the clerk.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd tell the clerk to take the pay stub to the store and ask what authorizes any deduction. Repeal itself takes nothing out of it, {presiding}.
author: Codex writer B

text: The store couldn't withhold it on the strength of this vote, {presiding}. I favor keeping the ban because of the fee that might be negotiated later.
author: Codex writer B

text: The first check after repeal could look exactly like the last one, {presiding}. My concern is what management and the local could agree to later.
author: Codex writer B

text: Take the ballot question to the local, {presiding}. Repeal deals with bargaining over costs and leaves the rules for a ratification vote where they were.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd send the worker to the local's voting rules, {presiding}. Lifting a state ban on fees doesn't add a name to the ballot list.
author: Codex writer B

text: A fee isn't a ballot, {presiding}. That's one reason I'd keep the protection the worker has now.
author: Codex writer B

text: Taking a fee and giving out a ballot are separate decisions, {presiding}. Check the membership rules before promising the worker a vote.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd need the paragraph that sets our plants apart, {presiding}. Does it name this state outright or refer to whatever the law permits?
author: Codex writer B

text: Start with what the parties signed about this plant, {presiding}. I support repeal, but I don't get to cross out their exception from this desk.
author: Codex writer B

text: Start with the exception the parties signed, {presiding}. I'm voting against repeal because our crews know where they stand under the state ban.
author: Codex writer B

text: Does it name the plant, {presiding}, or does it follow the law wherever the employee works? Those words could give the steward different answers after repeal.
author: Codex writer B

text: Where the parties have a duty to bargain, the company could hear the proposal and counter, {presiding}. It wouldn't have to agree to a fee.
author: Codex writer B

text: There's room at a bargaining table for somebody to say they won't agree to a fee, {presiding}. Repeal would let both sides take up the subject.
author: Codex writer B

text: The company can reject the demand, {presiding}. My concern is that it could also accept one down the road, and then the worker has to live with it.
author: Codex writer B

text: No signature comes with repeal, {presiding}. I'm voting against it because management and the local could still settle on a required payment later.
author: Codex writer B

text: Let the member show us the page of the national agreement that covers our crews, {presiding}. I'd hear what they stand to lose before I take that term off the table.
author: Codex writer B

text: Somewhere a steward has to take this vote back to the shop and explain why the crew across the line can bargain for something this crew can't. I wouldn't ask that of them, {presiding}.
author: Codex writer B

text: The company wanted a national deal and the crew bargained for one, {presiding}. I'm against cutting a term out of it at the state line.
author: Codex writer B

text: Put yourself in the transfer office, {presiding}. Same company, same job, and now somebody has to walk the worker through a different fee rule. I'd leave the bargaining where it is.
author: Codex writer B

text: The supervisor skips over a nonmember when posting the schedule. Who has to take that complaint back to management, {presiding}? I'd let the people doing that work bargain over the cost.
author: Codex writer B

text: Members can vote the agreement down. Nonmembers may get the raise anyway. Why should we tell the bargaining team it can't propose sharing the expense, {presiding}?
author: Codex writer B

text: A grievance can take a steward off the floor for hours, {presiding}. The work still has to get done when the worker bringing it never took a union card.
author: Codex writer B

text: Ask who'll take the call from a worker outside the local when the company reads the contract differently. I'd hear that answer before backing a fee ban, {presiding}.
author: Codex writer B

text: The clerk who works nights may never meet the person who wrote the notice. Give that clerk a name to call and a copy of the agreement. That's where I'd start, {presiding}.
author: Codex writer B

text: An unclear notice ought to come down, {presiding}. I can say that to the store without taking a fee proposal away from the bargaining team.
author: Codex writer B

text: What was on the wall when the clerk started, {presiding}, and what did the manager tell them? Barring a fee won't tell us whether the store explained the agreement honestly.
author: Codex writer B

text: The store and the local could sit down with a new hire and explain the fee together. I'd rather have that conversation at the store than settle it for them here, {presiding}.
author: Codex writer B

text: If a fee is a bad deal, management can turn it down, {presiding}. I'd rather see both sides at the table than have this house refuse the proposal before they meet.
author: Codex writer B

text: What do we think happens at a bargaining table, {presiding}? The employer can push back. The union can revise its demand. I want both of them to have that chance.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd like the people working that shift to hear what each side offered, {presiding}. They should get to judge the bargain instead of hearing from us that it never could be made.
author: Codex writer B

text: Suppose the employer would accept a fee in exchange for something the crew wants. How can we know from these desks what they'd be willing to trade, {presiding}?
author: Codex writer B
